walkthroughs.body_html:
Our system: Sun, 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.

The Sun is in the Milky Way galaxy.

Orbits are kept by gravity providing centripetal force.

Closer orbits = faster speed.

Nebula -> protostar -> main sequence.

Lower mass: red giant -> white dwarf.

Higher mass: red supergiant -> supernova -> neutron star or black hole.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
It is also longer, because both increase together.
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
